title: 5.4.8 Lab: Crash, and start again
description: Touching a pipe ends the round. Reuse the playing flag from 5.3.9: freeze the world when it ends, run the game only while the flag is true, and make the restart clear the pipes as well as the bird and the score.

steps.title: Touching a pipe ends the round
steps.instructions: Add a `playing` flag that starts `true`. Inside your pipe loop, test `bird.colliding(p)` and `bird.colliding(p.mate)`; when either one is true, set `playing` to `false`.
hints: `let playing` goes next to `score`, and `playing = true;` goes in `setup()`.
Both halves matter: the gap is between them, so a bird that hits only the bottom half must also lose.

steps.title: Freeze the world
steps.instructions: At the moment of the crash, inside the same `if` that sets the flag, stop everything that moves: set `world.gravity.y = 0`, `bird.vel.y = 0`, and every pipe's `vel.x` and its mate's `vel.x` to 0.
hints: A second loop inside that `if` reaches every pipe: `for (const q of pipes) { q.vel.x = 0; q.mate.vel.x = 0; }`.
The pipes stop because their speed becomes 0; the bird stops because gravity is off.

steps.title: Play only while playing
steps.instructions: Freezing stops what is already on the screen, but the code that makes new things still runs every frame: new pipes keep arriving on the beat, the space bar still flaps, and the score can still go up. Wrap the play code in `draw()` (the flap, the edge check, the new pipes on the beat, and both pipe loops) in `if (playing) { ... }`, the same shape as 5.3.10. Then draw 'Game over' in `drawTop()`, the function at the bottom of the starter that already shows the score: it runs after the pipes are drawn, so a frozen pipe cannot cover the words. Run it and crash: no new pipe should appear and the score should stay where it was.
hints: In `drawTop()`: `if (!playing) { text('Game over', 130, 190); }`. The `!` reads as "not", as in `!wasTouching` from 5.3.7. An `else` after `if (playing)` in `draw()` works too, but there a pipe can sit on top of the words.

steps.title: Put back everything a round owns
steps.instructions: When R is pressed, put the world back for a fresh round: delete every pipe and empty the array, reset the bird's position and speed, turn gravity back on, zero the score, and set `playing = true`.
hints: Empty the array only after deleting each sprite: loop with `for (const p of pipes) { p.mate.delete(); p.delete(); }` and then `pipes = [];`.
Put the R check after the whole `if (playing) { ... }`, not inside it, or it can never run once the round is over.
Forget the pipes and the old ones are still sliding in the next round.

requirements.title: A flag says whether the game is being played
requirements.description: A variable that starts true is the game's state. Help: 5.3.9 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: Touching a pipe ends the round
requirements.description: A collision with the bird flips the flag (playing = false, or a game-over flag = true). Help: 5.3.9 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: The crash freezes the world
requirements.description: Gravity goes to 0 and the pipes stop too (their vel.x goes to 0), so nothing keeps moving. The bird's own vel.x line from the starter does not count: it is the pipes that must stop. Help: 5.4.5 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: The game runs only while the flag is true
requirements.description: The play code, including the new pipes on the beat, sits inside if (playing), so nothing new happens after a crash. Help: 5.3.9 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: Game over shows when the round ends
requirements.description: While the flag is false, the screen says Game over. Help: 5.3.9 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: The restart clears the pipes
requirements.description: Pressing R empties the array so the next round starts clean. Help: 5.4.5 (Reading: A world that scrolls)
